profile_name: Named Murder Case — 911 Cold Open, Warm Victim Portrait
based_on: A faceless English channel about single named American murder cases (~3,400 words, 23 minutes, AI narration over case photos and drone/stock footage). No names, places or cases from the original are kept.
best_for: one domestic or small-town murder per video, 20–30 minutes; extendable to 45–60 minutes when the case has a trial

point_of_view.narration: third-person, present tense in the cold open, past tense afterwards
point_of_view.viewer_address: light second person in asides ('Honestly, everyone knows each other') and in the closing call-to-action
point_of_view.first_person: only 'we' for the channel at the end

audience_addressing_style: invisible narrator with a few conversational asides; one call-to-action at the very end

hook_style.type: date + place + 'a normal, quiet day' + the emergency call, quoted line by line
hook_style.formula: [Full date], [Town], [State]. Just a normal, quiet day. Then a 911 call comes in. [Short exchange with the dispatcher, real documented words]. [What responders find, in clinical detail without gore]. [A detective's first doubt, quoted].

narrative_structure.type: 911 cold open → town portrait → victim biography → the relationship → the day itself → the investigation's doubts → digital and forensic evidence → the suspect's mind → interviews → trial → reflective ending on trust and community
beats_in_order: 2. Town portrait: 'the sort of town where people settle in and don't leave', families, churches, generations on the same jobs.
3. Victim biography from birth: family size, how the town remembered her, what she gave to others, a sentence everybody repeated about her.
4. The relationship with the suspect and the cracks nobody saw.
5. The morning or day of the death, reconstructed.
6. The detail that 'didn't seem right' to investigators.
7. Evidence: scene analysis, phone and computer searches, timelines.
8. A passage that reads the suspect's thinking ('That is a very specific kind of thinking…'), anchored in evidence.
11. Reflection on what the case leaves in a close community, then the victim's full name, age and a closing line about saying her name correctly.

pacing.overall: measured and even; short factual sentences in sequence
pacing.acceleration: the evidence section stacks facts quickly
pacing.pause_points: after the victim portrait and after the verdict

sentence_style.mix: mostly short and medium declaratives; occasional one-line verdicts ('He was almost right.')
sentence_style.questions: rhetorical questions only inside quoted investigators' doubts
sentence_style.repetition: anaphora in the analysis of the suspect ('He knew… He knew… He knew…')

language_style.humanising_detail: small community details: Little League teams, church bulletins, wakes, local funeral homes

characters.victim: the emotional centre, described through what others said about her
characters.suspect: a trusted insider (spouse, officer, relative); his expertise turned against the truth
characters.investigators: named detectives with their first doubts quoted
characters.community: the town that learns trust guarantees nothing

dialogue.use: real 911 audio lines, investigator interviews, court testimony
dialogue.format_in_script: written as plain sentences inside the narration; never invented
dialogue.frequency: a dense block in the hook, then 1–2 quotes per part

emotional_tone.arc: ordinary calm → shock → warmth for the victim → suspicion → cold clarity → justice → sober reflection

common_devices: 'Just a normal, quiet day.' contrast opener
victim remembered through a sentence everyone repeated
reading the suspect's mindset from his own searches and actions
one-line verdicts after long passages ('He was almost right.')
closing line about keeping the victim's name alive

call_to_action_style.closing: 'If this story stayed with you, share it. It matters that [victim]'s name keeps being said, and said correctly. If you'd like to support the channel, liking, sharing and subscribing is the best way.'

visual_cue_prompts.note: Not written in the final script; for the shot list only.
visual_cue_prompts.hook: 911 audio waveform with typed transcript, house exterior, police lights
visual_cue_prompts.town: drone shots of the real town, main street, church, school
visual_cue_prompts.victim: real family photos with depth parallax, name and age lower third
visual_cue_prompts.evidence: highlighted search history, timeline graphic, floor plan of the room

safety_and_compliance: Only documented quotes; 911 audio used briefly and commented.
No gore; one plain sentence for the wound or cause of death.
No AI likeness of the victim; no minors recreated.

script_formatting_rules.parts: The final script must be sectioned into 10 parts, each part at least 800 words.
script_formatting_rules.total_length: The full script must be 8,000+ words in total.
script_formatting_rules.no_headings: No section headings, no part numbers, no titles inside the text.
script_formatting_rules.no_line_breaks: No line breaks: the whole script is one continuous block of text.
script_formatting_rules.no_symbols: No underscores, no bullet points, no brackets, no stage directions, no visual cues, no comments.
script_formatting_rules.no_wrappers: No introductory statement and no closing statement outside the narration itself.
script_formatting_rules.delivery: Send the whole script in one batch, only the script text, with nothing before or after it.
